markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

1. **Context retention:** Supplied matched-prefix probes reduce margins across all datasets. Retain history provisionally; these checkpoint interventions do not establish cropped-training performance.
2. **Implementation validity:** Every padding check exceeds its declared tolerance; Electronics reaches 0.00234. Investigate semantic errors and numerical variation before interpreting context effects.
3. **Evidence limits:** Feedback favors recent, specific matches. Interactions cannot establish ownership, compatibility, purchase readiness, or preference drift.
4. **Recurrent semantics:** [GRU equations](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html) permit padding-induced state updates. [Packing](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence.html) requires chronological compaction; [numerical differences](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html) alone do not establish incorrect recurrence.
5. **Attribution validity:** [TimeSHAP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.00073) motivates recurrent attribution; the [faithfulness survey](https://aclanthology.org/2024.cl-2.6/) cautions about erasure-induced distribution shifts. Sensitivity does not establish useful memory or intent.
6. **Evaluation validity:** [Krichene–Rendle](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2021/651) show sampled metrics can distort comparisons. [GRU4Rec reproducibility research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.14956) motivates measuring implementation changes independently.

### Framework and candidate ideas

Organize work into implementation validity, controlled context intervention, and attribution validation. Later stages require interpretable earlier measurements.

| Idea | Mechanism | Originality: positive / negative | Potential: positive / negative | Difficulty: favorable / challenging |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Padding audit and conditional repair** | Compact, pack, restore alignment | **3:** diagnostic integration / established semantics | **7:** removes a confound / gain uncertain | **5:** standard APIs / reference and predictor integration |
| Matched suffix experiment | Compare full/all-target, full/matched-target, cropped/matched-target conditions | **4:** separates supervision / familiar augmentation | **7:** tests context utility / costly comparison | **4:** simple masks / candidate and RNG matching |
| Prefix-order audit | Shuffle older events; fix suffix and candidates | **4:** tests order sensitivity / artificial perturbation | **6:** guides memory design / cannot infer intent | **3:** inference-only / uncertainty needs care |

Scores are qualitative; difficulty increases with implementation effort. [CL4SRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.14395) motivates augmentation, but its contrastive objective does not isolate supervised cropping.

### Selected idea: padding audit before cropping

At 20% progress, prioritize this falsifiable intervention. Freeze fixtures and tolerances before testing. Compare identical weights in evaluation mode, without autocast, against a float64 padding-skipping reference matching PyTorch’s reset-gate equation.

```text
extract chronological nonzero inputs and original positions
separate empty rows; compact remaining rows into valid prefixes
pack with positive CPU int64 lengths; run existing GRU from zero state
unpack; map valid outputs bijectively to original B × L positions
read greatest nonpadding index; preserve empty-history policy
```

Compare leading-padding lengths, mixed batches, permutations, isolated execution, singleton histories, and unrelated successive calls. Predeclare FP32 atol=1e-5/rtol=1.3e-6 and FP64 both 1e-7 as starting thresholds, not guarantees. Report errors and failing-element counts; retain thresholds during precision/backend escalation. Audit reset boundaries, gradients, dropout, and checkpoint–predictor agreement. Preserve correct baseline behavior; retrain only if semantic repair is justified.

Keep full-history inference, baseline loss/optimizer/sampling, seeds 0/42, ≤200 epochs, 200 batches/epoch, four routes, diagnostic interfaces, and the shared GPU budget. Synchronize the predictor writer; deploy one checkpoint/category. Predeclare checkpoint selection and evaluate complete conditions using pinned macro validation HR@10. Track target exposures, tokens, and GPU seconds. No gain, full-catalog improvement, or seed robustness is established; repeated validation selection risks overfitting.

idea.description: Audit padding invariance in the supplied corrected GRU4Rec against an explicit padding-skipping reference, and conditionally replace semantically padding-sensitive execution with compacted packed recurrence. Preserve the GRU backbone, aligned sequence features, full-history inference, and exactly one independently trained checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: All four supplied padding checks exceed their declared absolute tolerance, confounding interpretation of context-removal effects. These discrepancies warrant investigation but do not prove an implementation bug: batching, precision and backend algorithms can produce numerical differences. At 20% research progress, establishing recurrent execution semantics is more informative than immediately introducing another recency mechanism. The reported negative context-removal margins also argue against assuming that older history is harmful.
idea.implementation_notes:
Treat this as an implementation-validity study, with no measured validation improvement yet. Originality 3, future potential 7 and code difficulty 5 are qualitative scores; higher difficulty means greater implementation effort. Prioritize the audit, retain the matched-suffix experiment as the next controlled study, and use prefix-order attribution only after recurrence is interpretable.

Before inspecting audit results, freeze training-only fixtures covering empty, singleton, short and maximum-length histories; varied leading-padding lengths; mixed-length companions; batch permutations; repeated identical calls; and successive unrelated histories. Freeze identical parameters and initial states. Run in evaluation mode with autocast disabled. Compare aligned valid-token features, final states, identical candidate scores, relative L2 error, maximum absolute error, failing-element counts, top-10 overlap and target-rank changes. Record margins near rank 10 to identify tie-sensitive flips. Repeated identical execution measures nondeterminism but cannot detect a deterministic padding bias.

Implement a diagnostic float64 recurrence using the existing GRU weights and PyTorch's exact equations: gate order reset/update/new, with the reset gate multiplying the recurrent candidate affine transform including its recurrent bias. At each layer, update hidden state only for valid tokens and otherwise preserve it. Reset every independent example to the baseline initial state. Compare this reference with individually unpadded execution and compacted packed execution. A dense padded GRU may intentionally differ because its biases and recurrent transformations execute on padding. A reference implementation is itself fallible, so verify it against unpadded native GRU execution before treating it as authoritative.

Predeclare elementwise |actual-reference| <= atol + rtol*|reference|, initially using FP32 atol=1e-5 and rtol=1.3e-6, and FP64 atol=rtol=1e-7. These documented general testing defaults are starting thresholds rather than GRU accuracy guarantees. Keep thresholds fixed when investigating failures: repeat with TF32 explicitly disabled, then cuDNN disabled, then CPU float64. Record software, device and backend settings. Persistent padding-dependent disagreement with the verified reference supports a semantic problem; shrinking disagreement at higher precision supports a numerical explanation without proving correctness. Preserve the supplied corrected baseline when it passes these checks. Do not change tolerances after seeing validation outcomes.

If repair is justified, extract chronological nonzero tokens and retain their original row/position mapping. Separate empty rows; bypass packing for an entirely empty batch. Right-pad compacted nonempty rows and provide strictly positive one-dimensional CPU int64 lengths with enforce_sorted=False. Unpacking and returned h_n already restore input batch order; do not unsort twice. Use total_length=L, then restore external left-padded alignment by indexing valid positions only. Require a bijection between compacted valid outputs and original valid positions. Never scatter padded entries using clamped duplicate destinations. If scatter_ is used, satisfy its backward shape requirements and ensure unique valid destinations. Preserve the baseline empty-history feature/scoring policy explicitly.

Retain the same embeddings, recurrent layers, output transforms and scoring semantics. Audit input/output dropout placement and mask reuse; GRU built-in dropout only operates between recurrent layers and does nothing for a single layer. Packing can change dropout draws and the training trajectory, so equal seeds do not imply equal stochastic realizations. Check finite, nonzero gradients on a nondegenerate fixture for retained embeddings and recurrent parameters, correct output-target alignment, no cross-example state leakage, truncation/detachment boundaries, and train/eval behavior. Read the greatest nonpadding index in the original representation, never count minus one; length minus one is valid only in the compacted prefix representation.

Retain item_emb, log2feats(sequence) returning aligned B x L x H features, predict_score(features, items), ModelView, and view.model as the actual trained nn.Module. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Handle (None, sequence, positive, negative) batches with matching B x L tensors; restore model mode and return measured metrics plus metric_definitions. Report unsupported or absent measurements as unavailable. Update the embedded predictor writer with identical recurrence, alignment, reset and readout behavior; verify checkpoint/predictor feature and score agreement on fixed fixtures.

Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing; DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; artifacts beneath the trial directory; preprocessing seed 0; training seed 42; at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Preserve baseline loss, optimizer, negative sampling, batch size and schedule for this intervention. Predeclare a common affordable epoch count E<=200 and final-epoch checkpoint selection for any baseline-versus-repair comparison, before condition scores are observed. Use the corrected cold start in this trial rather than another trial's checkpoint. If the complete comparison cannot fit the remaining budget, report that limitation; an audit alone is not an accuracy comparison. Charge all training, diagnostics, debugging and failed attempts to the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget; each run remains single-GPU, and concurrent slots do not enlarge the allowance.

Train one independent model per category in each separately evaluated condition. Deploy only the selected condition's four category checkpoints; never average, fuse, vote, stack or combine separately fitted auxiliary scores. Select complete conditions using unchanged host macro validation HR@10 with its pinned 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42; predeclare baseline preference for exact ties. Record supervised-target exposures, processed tokens, optimizer steps and GPU seconds. Generate required full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five real training users/category, but do not substitute these for host validation or claim full-catalog gains from sampled HR@10.

For later cropping research, apply repaired execution uniformly to full/all-target, full/matched-target and cropped/matched-target conditions. Match original batches, retained target plans, negatives, loss denominators and update counts between the latter two. Keep targets outside their causal input prefixes and preserve target adjacency. Record supervision differences from the all-target baseline. CL4SRec motivates augmentation but does not establish a benefit for this supervised-only intervention. A shuffle-prefix audit holds suffix and candidates fixed but still uses artificial histories.

Use only permitted histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps. Ratings, review text, item categories, prices, stores and simulator traits are unavailable despite generic upstream examples. Interactions do not establish ownership, compatibility or intent. Padding-correlated shortcuts are a hypothesis to test; removing padding dependence does not eliminate popularity, length or other shortcuts. Predeclared fixtures, interventions and selection rules reduce adaptive validation overfitting, but seed-42-only comparisons do not establish seed robustness. If host per-user hits are available, paired within-category bootstrap intervals can describe conditional validation-user uncertainty; aggregate scores cannot recover these intervals, and they exclude training-seed, candidate-sampling and adaptive-selection uncertainty.
idea.pseudocode:
predeclare fixtures, tolerances, backend escalation, affordable E<=200,
200 batches/epoch, final-epoch checkpoints, and baseline-first tie rule

freeze supplied corrected GRU weights and initial-state policy
verify float64 padding-skipping reference against native unpadded GRU:
    use PyTorch gate equations, including reset-after-recurrent-affine semantics
    reset hidden states for each independent history
    preserve each layer's state whenever input position is padding

audit in eval mode with autocast disabled:
    compare varied leading padding, isolated/mixed/permuted batches,
            singleton histories, repeated calls and unrelated successive calls
    compare valid-token features, final features, candidate scores and ranks
    report absolute/relative errors and fixed-threshold failure counts
    on failure, retain thresholds and escalate precision/backend controls

if verified evidence requires a semantic repair:
    valid = sequence != 0
    nonempty_rows = rows with at least one valid token
    preserve explicit baseline empty-history behavior
    if nonempty_rows exist:
        gather real tokens chronologically and remember original positions
        right-pad compacted histories to width L
        lengths = positive CPU int64 vector
        packed = pack_padded_sequence(compact, lengths,
                                      batch_first=True, enforce_sorted=False)
        packed_outputs, h_n = existing_GRU(packed, fresh_zero_state)
        compact_outputs = unpack(packed_outputs, total_length=L)
        # PyTorch already restores input batch order.
        map only valid outputs bijectively to original B x L positions
        preserve original embedding/output/dropout/scoring semantics
    read greatest original nonpadding index; handle empty rows separately
    verify alignment, gradients, reset boundaries and predictor agreement
    train one independent repaired GRU4Rec per required category
    compare with a complete baseline condition only if budget permits
else:
    preserve the supplied corrected baseline

return measured diagnostic metrics and definitions; restore model mode
host scores complete conditions with the unchanged pinned macro HR@10
select one condition; deploy exactly one checkpoint for each category
use full permitted histories at prediction; never fuse models or scores

originality.positive: Combines family-specific metamorphic checks, a verified recurrent reference and a controlled execution intervention to address a concrete confound in context experiments.
originality.negative: Packing, padding masks, reference recurrences and invariance checks are established techniques; the contribution is an experimental protocol rather than a new recommendation algorithm.

future_potential.positive: Reliable recurrence can make later supervision and context-retention experiments interpretable, and the audit can transfer to other recurrent recommendation implementations.
future_potential.negative: The corrected baseline may already be semantically valid, the protocol has no demonstrated accuracy benefit, and broader adoption depends on showing reproducible practical value.

code_difficulty.positive: Standard PyTorch packing APIs preserve the GRU parameters and scoring architecture, and the diagnostic reference can remain separate from deployment.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact gate semantics, backend comparisons, empty rows, differentiable output remapping, dropout behavior and embedded predictor consistency require substantial care.

related_work.title: PyTorch GRU documentation
contributions: Documents gate equations, including PyTorch's placement of the reset gate after the recurrent candidate affine transformation.
Explains recurrent biases and between-layer dropout semantics relevant to padding and reproducibility.
limitations: Provides execution semantics rather than evidence that a repair improves this benchmark.
Built-in dropout does not implement explicit input/output dropout and has no effect with one recurrent layer.

related_work.title: PyTorch pack_padded_sequence documentation
contributions: Provides packed recurrence for variable-length valid prefixes using positive lengths.
Supports execution after chronological compaction of externally left-padded histories.
limitations: Unmodified left-padded arrays cannot be packed correctly using nonzero counts alone.
Empty rows require separate handling, and unpacked outputs must be mapped back to original positions.

related_work.title: TimeSHAP: Explaining Recurrent Models through Sequence Perturbations
contributions: Provides a reference for event attribution and temporal pruning in recurrent models.
limitations: Does not establish that deletion reveals actual intent or improves GRU4Rec validation ranking.
Perturbation sensitivity requires separate interpretation from useful predictive memory.

related_work.title: Faithfulness survey supplied in the research context
contributions: Highlights limitations of erasure-based explanation evaluation, including distribution shifts.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed recurrent reference, padding audit or matched-context experiment for this task.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation — Krichene and Rendle
contributions: Analyzes inconsistencies in sampled recommendation metrics that can affect model ordering.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned evaluator.
A sampled HR@10 improvement here does not establish full-catalog improvement.

related_work.title: PyTorch numerical accuracy notes
contributions: Explains floating-point variation across batched, individual, device and backend executions.
Motivates precision-controlled diagnosis before attributing discrepancies to semantic errors.
limitations: Does not supply a universal GRU error bound or prove that any observed discrepancy is harmless.

related_work.title: PyTorch testing documentation
contributions: Defines elementwise absolute-plus-relative comparisons and dtype-specific assert_close defaults.
limitations: General defaults are starting thresholds rather than guaranteed tolerances for recurrent computations.

related_work.title: PyTorch CUDA backend precision controls
contributions: Documents backend precision settings relevant to controlled TF32 and numerical investigations.
limitations: Controls and defaults depend on the installed PyTorch version and hardware; disabling reduced precision does not establish semantic correctness.

related_work.title: PyTorch packing implementation
contributions: Details internal sorting and restoration of input order during packing and unpacking.
limitations: The linked main branch can differ from the installed version; record the actual runtime version.

related_work.title: PyTorch GRU implementation
contributions: Documents packed recurrent execution and restoration of returned hidden states to input order.
limitations: Implementation inspection does not replace task-specific alignment and state-reset checks.

related_work.title: PyTorch scatter_ documentation
contributions: Documents backward shape requirements and hazards associated with duplicate destination indices.
limitations: Correct scattering still requires an explicit bijection over valid sequence positions.

related_work.title: GRU4Rec reproducibility study supplied in the research context
contributions: Reports that implementation differences can materially affect GRU4Rec accuracy and runtime.
limitations: Does not establish that the supplied corrected baseline contains a padding bug or predict this intervention's validation effect.

related_work.title: Official GRU4Rec implementation
contributions: Provides a reference for GRU4Rec execution, optimization and session-oriented state handling.
limitations: Session boundaries and execution choices require adaptation to independently sampled user-history examples; copying them blindly would not preserve this benchmark's contract.

related_work.title: CL4SRec: Contrastive Learning for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Motivates sequence augmentation as a research direction using augmented views and contrastive learning.
limitations: Combines augmentation with an auxiliary contrastive objective and therefore does not isolate supervised context cropping.
Does not validate the proposed GRU4Rec cropping policy or matched-target control.
